title: By six months, most babies put things in the mouth to explore them
summary: The CDC says that by six months, most babies put things in the mouth to explore them.
body: Under cognitive milestones at six months, the CDC lists setting things in her mouth to explore them. Explore is the page's word for that line. It is one item for most babies by six months on the US list. It is not a feeding rule, and it is not the textbook sentence about testing whether something is edible. Exploration is the point of the six-month line, not a feeding rule.

sources.title: Milestones by 6 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the cognitive item 'Puts things in her mouth to explore them.'
